correctness.rationale: For b>0 and any compact invariant μ, coordinate antiderivatives give E[sin y|x]=bx and cyclic analogues. Thus residual speeds R_x=sin y−bx are conditionally orthogonal to receiving coordinates, yielding Var(sin y)=b²Var(x)+E[R_x²] and Cov(x,sin y)=b Var(x), likewise y,z. Since sin is one-Lipschitz, Var(sin Y)≤Var(Y); setting A,B,C as coordinate variances and U,V,W as speed squares yields B≥b² A+U, C≥b² B+V, A≥b² C+W. Sum proves U+V+W≤(1−b²)(A+B+C); cyclic substitution gives b^4 U+b² V+W≤(1−b^6)A and rotations. Checked substitution symbolic coefficients b^6 A+b^4 U+b²V+W exactly. Bounded backward variation of constants gives x(t)=∫_0∞ e^(-bs)sin y(t-s)ds and |x|≤1/b; no finite orbit tests used as proof.
residual_risks: Compact support invariant measures; the backward memory/cube applies to bounded complete trajectories.

originality.rationale: Direct full-text original 2007 Sprott–Chlouverakis paper analyzes precisely the sine cyclic flow, numerical standard deviations σ, kurtosis, chaos, multistability and orbit bifurcations; its displayed σ² is a trajectory average of x²+y²+z², not an all-invariant-measures conditional mean or exact mean-square-speed bound. Thomas 1999 original abstract treats circuits and labyrinth attractors. Resultary semantic checks showed the focal finding and related Chen-fiber stationary regressions but no stronger bound for this exact sine cycle. Although generator orthogonality and Lipschitz variance contraction are standard tools, their three-way cyclic coupling gives explicit directional b^4,b²,1 weighted budgets not implication-wise supplied by the cited numerical RMS analyses; best-of-knowledge original as a natural same-object bound.
residual_risks: The conditional generator calculation is short and might occur as a different statistical-energy argument in unindexed original literature.
Bounds do not establish sharp constants or characterize the recurrent measure; theorem is a structural stationary restriction only.

value.rationale: The Thomas flow exhibits coexisting attractors and nontrivial b-dependent variance. A uniform exact three-edge stationary calibration and global/directional a priori bounds on mean-square speed apply separately to every invariant measure, without symmetry or ergodicity. For 0<b<1 the bounds constrain active recurrent dynamics quantitatively, while b≥1 collapses stationary speed/variance and is already known; that threshold is NOT claimed as a new contribution. This is a motivated structural necessary constraint and numerical cross-check invariant, not a single unmotivated parameter value or claim of new bifurcation theory.
residual_risks: The conditional generator calculation is short and might occur as a different statistical-energy argument in unindexed original literature.
Bounds do not establish sharp constants or characterize the recurrent measure; theorem is a structural stationary restriction only.

scientific_limitations: Compact support invariant measures; the backward memory/cube applies to bounded complete trajectories.
Does not classify existence, uniqueness, bifurcations, entropy or chaos.
The b≥1 global-stability threshold is previously known and excluded from originality.
The correlation expression requires positive receiving-coordinate variance.
Directional bounds are not claimed optimal for each b.
